absent: Full layout of emulation context, virtual processor and virtual machine structures beyond the fields touched in these fragments.
Vendor specific behavior behind delegated hooks for cycle handling, exception delivery, address translation and compatibility checks.
Remainder of pending event processing after the shown first part, including injection of new exceptions, interrupts and nested transitions.
Numeric encodings of hypercall numbers, request identifiers, error codes, run flags and hardware message fields.
Locking contracts beyond the observed global mutex and read side mapping lookup, including allowed sleep and interrupt contexts.
Allocation, lifetime and teardown of emulation contexts and timekeeping workers outside the shown creation and notification paths.

Exact guest visible semantics of clock pairing and paravirtual timekeeping beyond success and failure conditions shown.

findings.text: A single static operation table provides the host side of the instruction emulator, binding generic guest access, control and fault handling requests to local adapter routines.
A globally visible hypercall emulation routine acts as the central guest hypercall entry, enforcing privilege and feature gating and either completing locally or forwarding to userspace.
Requesting exit from system management mode through the emulator always warns once and reports the operation as unhandleable, so no state change occurs.
Emulated triple fault handling has no local effect beyond flagging a triple fault request against the calling virtual processor for later processing.
Extended control register reads through the emulator succeed only for the primary feature mask selector and return the stored host value, while any other selector is reported as failure.
Extended control register writes through the emulator delegate entirely to the common host setter and propagate its result unchanged.
Marking the virtual machine as bugged is performed at most once per machine and moves the machine into both bugged and dead states.
Untagged address resolution returns its input unchanged when the vendor layer offers no hook, and otherwise delegates the translation to that vendor hook with context, address and flags.
Canonical address judgment through the emulator is the negation of the host noncanonical test for the calling processor, and guest physical page validity is likewise delegated to the host predicate.

General register access plus nonmaskable mask control plus system management mode query each derive the host processor from the emulation context and delegate to the corresponding raw register, vendor, or mode facility.

Clock related global walks hold the main virtual machine list mutex while iterating over every machine and its processors to flag clock or master clock updates and while restarting timekeeping snapshots.
Directed yield takes a read side critical section only for the lookup of the destination processor in the address mapping and releases it before attempting any yield that could block.

The emulation dispatch structure groups together handlers for register, memory, segment, descriptor, control, debug, timing, power and fault operations so the generic emulator can call into host state uniformly.
The clock pairing record written to guest memory conveys wall time seconds and subsecond parts together with an adjusted processor cycle value and cleared flag and reserved areas.
Fast output completion clears pending transfer state and then either finishes immediately when the guest instruction position has moved or advances past the emulated instruction.
Fast input completion checks for a single pending unit, tolerates guest position movement, finalizes the value with width dependent merging behavior, then advances past the instruction.

Hypercall handling captures arguments with width awareness, rejects unprivileged callers, dispatches feature gated services, and either returns a status locally or exits to userspace with a completion callback that restores the result and advances.

Pending event processing gives nested exits first consideration, then observes a strict re injection order favoring already injected exceptions over waiting exceptions over nonmaskable state over regular interrupts, requesting immediate re entry when the nested layer requires it.
Emulation context creation allocates a zeroed object from a dedicated cache, reports exhaustion to the log, links processor and context in both directions, and installs the shared operation table.

Processor frequency notifications filter by transition direction, synchronously refresh the stored cycle rate on each affected processor, and flag resident virtual processors for timekeeping updates, with online and offline paths refreshing or clearing the stored rate.

Host timekeeping changes refresh the shared snapshot and, when guests rely on a master clock that is no longer cycle based, defer invalidation through interrupt mediated work that ultimately flags every virtual processor.
A fast input completion invoked with a pending length other than one triggers a virtual machine bug check and fails the operation as an input output error.

Raising the cycle rate without forcing remote processors out of guest execution could let guests observe the clock appearing to retreat, so the update path kicks affected processors when upscaling across processors.

Coexistence of an already injected exception with a newly pending exception, and any use of the exception exit injection or pending indicators, signals a logic error and is reported through one time warnings.
The clock pairing service accepts only the wallclock type selector and reports any other clock type as unsupported without touching guest memory.
The shared processor run area communicates system management and nested guest mode membership together with interrupt injection readiness and saved interrupt, privilege and addressing state.
Processor compatibility requires that the checking processor be online, that its reserved control register bits match those of the boot processor, and that the vendor compatibility hook approve.
Paravirtual kick delivery sends a local interrupt message with remote read semantics to the physical destination named by the caller through the common interrupt delivery path.
Virtualized interrupt initialization selects an absent cause when the global feature is enabled and a disabled cause otherwise, records that cause, and initializes the associated update semaphore.

Hypercall instruction repair synthesizes an undefined opcode fault in the emulation context when the compatibility quirk is off, and otherwise installs vendor supplied replacement bytes at the current guest position.

After each run the host snapshots interrupt enablement, privilege level view, addressing base and readiness for interrupt delivery, and marks system management and nested guest membership in the shared area.
Exception injection suppresses any error code indication when the processor is outside protected mode and then delegates delivery to the vendor injection hook after tracing.

Hypervisor time resynchronization marks master clock progress on all machines, halts emulated cycle handling, aligns stored cycle rates when cycles are not invariant, and restarts per machine timekeeping updates under the global mutex.
The interrupt window request predicate is true only when userspace has asked for a window and the programmable interrupt logic is not owned by the kernel.
Exhaustion of the emulation context cache is logged as an error and propagated as a null result with no processor linkage established.
Directed yield counts every attempt, ignores single task execution, missing or unready destinations and self requests, and counts only a successful handoff to another ready processor as success.
Hypercall completion from userspace truncates the returned value to thirty two bits for narrow guests before storing it in the accumulator and advancing past the instruction.
Stored cycle rate selection prefers the frequency event value when present, then a fast frequency query, then the global fallback, and warns if the processor claims an invariant cycle counter.
Clock pairing refuses processors that always catch up and failures of host time capture, and reports guest memory write failures as guest faults while otherwise returning success.
